title.text: Tasks · Headings, list text and a clearer title

howto.text:
How to try it

• Press Play, then click inside once so it has the keys.
• PHYS 122 is the example: a course with notes, three headings with notes of their own, and a task before the first.
• ⌥⌘N (⌃⌥N here) adds a heading above the selected task. Double-click a heading or the title to rename it; Tab goes on to its notes.
• Space or the chevron collapses a heading. Drag a heading and its tasks come with it.

n_ctx.text: Headings stay in their list. Today, Upcoming, Undated, Completed and Trash never show one, as a row or on a task's row: a task there reads as it did before.

t_title.text: The list's title, its notes, and headings

n_title.text:
The list's name is a 20pt semibold title at the top of the list, after its tile, with the list's notes under it. Once it scrolls under the band, the band's own small title fades in. Today and the views get the same title line, without notes.

Headings are 13pt semibold with a hairline and 8pt of air above. A heading can have notes too, under it. All of it is Markdown in the notes editor, a step quieter than the tasks.

n_work.text:
⌥⌘N, or New Heading Above in a task's menu. Return names it; Esc or no name leaves nothing.

Collapsing folds a heading's notes and tasks up under it; expanding unfolds them from under it, on the same curve as the rows below. It's local to the Mac and never synced.

Deleting a heading keeps its tasks (they join the heading above). It doesn't go to Trash, and Undo brings it back.
